subject: Meteorology
title: How Tornadoes Form
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on How Tornadoes Form.

hook.text: A tornado begins when rotation in a supercell's mesocyclone tightens and stretches toward the ground.

buildup.text: As the rotating column narrows, it spins faster—like a figure skater pulling in their arms.

discovery.text: A funnel cloud becomes a tornado only when the rotating winds reach the surface and cause damage.

twist.text: The rear-flank downdraft may help wrap rotation downward—but exactly how tornadoes touch down is still debated.

climax.text: Understanding tornadogenesis remains one of meteorology's biggest unsolved problems—progress is slow and hard-won.

punchline.text: We can see them, track them—but birth moment is still a mystery.

quiz.question: When does a funnel cloud officially become a tornado?
